newsitem.title: LIBYA: African ministers set summit on Zaire conflict.
newsitem.headline: African ministers set summit on Zaire conflict.

text.p: The head of the Organisation of African Unity on Wednesday urged an immediate ceasefire in Zaire's civil war while member ministers said a summit on Zaire would be held next month.

"There have been many initiatives by African leaders...(and) despite these efforts, there has not been significant progress towards the restoration of peace in eastern Zaire," said OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim in his opening speech to the meeting of foreign ministers.
The special joint OAU and U.N. envoy on the Great Lakes crisis, Mohamed Sahnoun, is currently in South Africa where he is expected to have talks with Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
Kabila arrived in South Africa on Tuesday for what sources said were secret talks on a solution to the civil war, which Kabila's rebels say is aimed at toppling Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The African foreign affairs ministers on Wednesday decided on an urgent summit on the situation in Central Africa and especially in eastern Zaire, an OAU official said.
The site for the summit, scheduled for March 18-19 for African heads of state, has not yet been decided, Ibrahim Daggash told journalists.
"The summit will discuss the sitution in the Great Lakes region and especially in eastern Zaire," Daggash said.
The decision was taken ahead of the opening session of the OAU's annual ministerial conference, this year in Tripoli.

Salim suggested a seven-point peace plan, including a call for dialogue and negotiations by parties to the conflict, similar to the five-point plan endorsed by the U.N. Security Council in a resolution on February 18.

The U.N. plan calls for an immediate ceasefire, the withdrawal of all foreign forces from Zaire including mercenaries hired by the government, and for Zaire's sovereignty and territory to be respected.
"Further deterioration of the situation in Zaire would have dire consequences impacting seriously on humanitarian, economic and political stability in the continent," Salim said.
